summary: Emerald Commerce - multiplexed streaming silence causing duplicate completions and billing exposure (post-incident action plan)
description: Issue summary: During a high-throughput marketing push, Emerald Commerce observed a multi-region degradation in multiplexed streaming where long-lived multiplexed sessions entered a silent state for several seconds, then replayed/duplicated completions when the stream resumed. Impact: duplicate completions led to increased per-token billing (customer-visible invoice exposure) and inconsistent application behavior for checkout flows. Environment: production (us-east-1) using multiplexed streaming over HTTP/2 to redwood-open-13B-quant-v2 pinned model. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create multiplexed session with 200 concurrent client streams. 2) Send a range of short prompt batches with intermittent small payload delays. 3) Observe transient stream silence ~2-6s followed by repeated completion frames. Observed logs: streaming-reset followed by completion-replay traces, per-request UUIDs repeated in audit logs, and billing meter reporting tokens counted twice for affected request IDs.
timeline: 2026-03-06 01:12 UTC - Emerald Commerce reported higher-than-normal invoice for peak window and intermittent checkout errors (SUP inbound).
2026-03-06 01:30 UTC - Support triaged as P0; engaged SRE and Billing. First response to customer acknowledged impact and requested traces.
2026-03-06 02:05 UTC - Initial hypothesis: client-side retries + server-side replay due to idle connection reattachment. SRE collected multiplex logs and proxy traces.
2026-03-06 03:10 UTC - Identified pattern: upstream streaming proxy emitted a keepalive gap; runtime suppressed a retransmit flag and later re-sent completion frames without marking as duplicate.
2026-03-06 04:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation deployed: server-side dedup filter on request UUID + short token credit hold to avoid immediate double-billing; customer notified.
2026-03-06 10:30 UTC - Billing team applied a manual credit for the affected window and confirmed invoice adjustment; customer received confirmation.
2026-03-07 09:00 UTC - Permanent fix merged: ensure idempotency flags are preserved across proxy reconnects and add defensive duplicate-suppression in billing pipeline (PRs linked).
2026-03-14 15:00 UTC - Post-incident follow-up meeting completed; action items assigned and timeline published to customer.
2026-03-14 16:00 UTC - Ticket moved to Resolved after verification with Emerald Commerce that retries ceased and billing credit accepted.
investigation_notes: Logs show repeated completion frames with identical request_uuid headers for multiplex participants; timestamps indicate a gap of 2-6s before duplication.
Proxy (edge-nginx-mlproxy) emitted a keepalive probe failure that caused connection rebind. Session rebind logic lacked propagation of idempotency metadata to new stream context.
Serving runtime did not mark retransmitted completions as duplicates because the idempotency token field was stored in ephemeral memory tied to the previous stream context.
Billing pipeline ingested both completion events before duplicate detection fired; dedup window too short for the observed gap.
Customer-side logs show no explicit client retries; behaviour is server-side replay rather than client-initiated retransmit in majority of traces.
Reproduced locally with a scripted connection-clobber at the proxy layer; confirmed duplicate completions when idempotency metadata is lost.

resolution: Short-term mitigation: deployed server-side dedup filter for request_uuid and temporarily held duplicate token charges pending review.
Billing action: issued manual credit for the affected invoice window and prevented auto-invoice reconciliation for that account until fixes were validated.
Permanent fix: patched proxy rebind logic to carry x-redwood-idempotency through stream reconnects and extended billing dedup window to 10s; patches merged to main (PRs linked).
Deployment plan: canary rollout in us-east-1 on 2026-03-16 followed by gradual rollout to other regions; monitoring dashboards added for duplicate completions and mux keepalive gaps.
Verification: Emerald Commerce validated the fix in their acceptance tests; SRE observed no duplicate completions in 72-hour post-rollout sample.
Status: Resolved. Customer received credit and post-incident report; follow-up tasks remain for cross-region hardening.
